clue.text: Circle newspaper article revealing chief troublemaker in group

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's main editorial article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece exposes who is stirring up trouble in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who instigates and heads a band of troublemakers.

clue.text: Fierce criminal in Brazilian port

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent out of its proper shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent criminal is at large in a South American seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Recife is a major seaport city on the north-east coast of Brazil.

clue.text: Common girl's language, initially

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name; the 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A remark on the everyday way a young woman talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and common are both used of what is ordinary, usual and unremarkable.

clue.text: Maths exercise causing lengthy disagreement

parts.note: long is a synonym of lengthy
a division is a split or disagreement between parties

explanation.surface: A pupil's arithmetic homework leads to a long-running quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Long division is a pencil-and-paper arithmetic method taught in school for dividing large numbers.

clue.text: Area in court to be renovated? On the contrary

indicators.note: renovating something means rebuilding it, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether part of a courtroom is due for refurbishment and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay and the answer phrase follows as its own reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Au contraire is French, borrowed into English, meaning on the contrary.

clue.text: River in Sussex, England

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of Sussex plus the start of England

explanation.surface: A geography note locating a river in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in southern England; the river named actually flows through Devon, not Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river in south-west England that reaches the sea at Exmouth.

clue.text: A cat, ounce

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A list pairing a domestic cat with an ounce, which is also a big cat (the snow leopard).
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is another name for the snow leopard, so the surface reads as two cats; here it means a tiny quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a very small amount, as in not an ounce or not an atom of truth.

clue.text: In which one may see Ping, Pang and Pong go round a point

definitions.text: In which one may see Ping, Pang and Pong

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one piece wraps the one after it

explanation.surface: Three silly-named characters are imagined spinning around a fixed spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ping, Pang and Pong sound like nonsense but are the three ministers in Puccini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Turandot is Puccini's opera whose cast includes the court officials Ping, Pang and Pong.

clue.text: Potential army leak? Nonsense

indicators.note: potential describes what something could become, so these letters may be turned into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Talk of a possible security leak from the military is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey is informal for foolish talk or humbug.

clue.text: Very bad, the French records

parts.note: chronic is informal for very bad

explanation.surface: A complaint that French record-keeping is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles are historical records of events set down in the order they happened.

clue.text: Artist's line after nothing said

indicators.note: after places the artist and line behind the word for nothing, so that piece goes second

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; the 's links it to the next word
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A painter's outline is drawn after nothing at all has been spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the artist and line behind the nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Make a short speech, or be taciturn about article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a taciturn person says few words

explanation.surface: A choice between giving a brief address and staying almost silent on a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To say a few words is the idiom for giving a short informal speech.

clue.text: Swindle German woman and daughter

parts.note: Frau is German for woman or wife
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A German mother and her daughter cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a deception or con carried out for gain, the noun sense of swindle.

clue.text: One in bar ordered drop of rum — that's something requiring little thought

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are set out in a new sequence
a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub orders a tot of rum, an easy decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is an informal term for a choice or task so obvious it needs hardly any thought.

clue.text: Dish — nuts left in mine

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, nuts

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A recipe of nuts abandoned in a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an ingredient but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert of a halved banana with ice cream and toppings.

clue.text: Besides displaying bravado, one is struggling against second in league

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
second in picks out the letter at position two of the word

explanation.surface: A team showing swagger is fighting against the side placed second in the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece, including the V and the E, goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and above is an idiom meaning in addition to, which is what besides means.

clue.text: One supporting the Treasury wielding party axe?

indicators.note: wielding means swinging something about, so the letters are swung into a new order

explanation.surface: A government backer imagined brandishing a political party's hatchet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Treasury is the UK government department in charge of public money.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxpayer funds the public purse, so is literally one who keeps the Treasury going.

clue.text: In the morning they changed stone for a purple variety of sapphire

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Some people swapped a stone for a purple sapphire one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' looks like a gem but is the unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental amethyst is a jeweller's name for violet-coloured sapphire.

clue.text: It's nothing to get in? Not right, there's this charge

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is to be left out of the phrase

parts.note: if it costs nothing to enter, admission is free
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone assumes entry is free and is told no, there is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission fee is the price paid for entry, a charge in the sense of a cost.

clue.text: A jolly girl in navy

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman serves in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the girl; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a navy, from the Spanish word.

clue.text: Leave course, disheartened

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: dessert is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their path, feeling dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a route; it is the meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or leave, especially a post or duty.

clue.text: Spy on the awfully small witch

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep watch on a tiny, wicked witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pythoness is a female soothsayer or witch, after the priestess of Apollo at Delphi.

clue.text: Had on about son being poorer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: if you had clothes on, you wore them
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent nagging about a son who is worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, so it means of lower quality, poorer.

clue.text: Toy boy losing head twice, flipping

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards
losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: an instruction to write the beheaded word two times in a row; it supplies no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A toyboy, a young lover, is decapitated twice and somersaulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' means the headless boy is written two times in a row before the whole is flipped. A toy boy is a young man going out with an older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spool-shaped toy that runs up and down a string.

clue.text: Dora lit me a fresh cigarette

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dora lights a new cigarette for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the cigarette, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor-made is slang for a factory-made cigarette, as opposed to a hand-rolled one.

clue.text: Head of Assembly, shot in the past

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: The head of a legislature was gunned down some time back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in the past, as in long ago.

clue.text: Sounds like legal documents for top hotel

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the word that follows

parts.note: writs are formal legal orders from a court

explanation.surface: Court papers are linked to a luxury hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London, a byword for the top end.

clue.text: Player against international, an opener for Trinidad

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cricketer facing an international side, opening the batting for Trinidad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a batsman; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is anyone taking part in a game or competition, a player.
